newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte and 18 parliamentarians visit Vavuniya welfare centre after complaints of lack of basic facilities. Occupants say welfare centres are like open jails.
Air force mounts air strikes on LTTE bases in Batticaloa.
Badulla-Colombo train service suspended owing to fear of terrorist attacks.
Defence Ministry advises military to ensure troops do not commit human rights abuses in areas they control.

Tax collection in 1995 was an "impressive" 74 billion rupees, accounting for 54 percent of government revenue and contributing 12.5 percent to Gross National Product, Commissioner General of Inland Revenue D.S. Weeraratne says.

Opposition United National Party ruled North Western Provincial Council to challenge budget proposals to legalise gambling and restrict operation of casinos to selected hotels on grounds that it is devolved subject.
Army finds large stocks of bombs and ammunition hidden by Tamil Tiger rebels in Valikamam in Jaffna peninsula on tip off given by public.
LTTE Sea Tiger leader Soosai arrives in Vakarai to mount attacks on security forces during Heroes' Week, senior army official says.
Paris Aid Group gives Sri Lanka $860 million in aid for 1997.
